mechanism_narrative: A rising quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates a strengthening economy, leading to higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth rate in the prior quarter is positive but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 0.5%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which drives consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of industrial production contraction (INDPRO < 95), the S&P 500 tends to decline in the following 60 days as a recession signal materializes.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 95 but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures that lead to higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL increases but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 550,000 units, it signals a strong housing market that boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST > 550.0 but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a strong consumer economy with accommodative monetary policy, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS increases and FEDFUNDS decreases but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 9.0%), the S&P 500 tends to decline in the following 5 days as economic weakness weighs on corporate earnings.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 9.0 but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases.
